body_markdown:
## How to Connect Lead Enrichment Tools to Instantly: The Short Answer


Connecting lead enrichment tools to Instantly means building and enriching your lead list *before* you touch the sequencing platform. Instantly is a sequencing engine — it sends emails, manages inboxes, and tracks replies. It does not find leads, verify emails, or enrich contacts. Every campaign you run in Instantly is only as good as what you put into it upstream.


The workflow is: **build list → enrich → verify → export → sequence** . Skip or rush any of those steps and you pay for it in bounces, low reply rates, and domain damage.


This guide walks through each step with enough specificity to actually execute it.


---


## Step 1: Build a Lead List Worth Enriching


Before you connect anything to Instantly, you need a list of contacts that match your ICP. That means job title, company size, industry, and ideally a buying signal — a reason this person is relevant *right now* .


If you're starting from scratch, a[lead generation agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/lead-generation-agent) can pull contacts from LinkedIn intelligence, company databases, Google Maps, or custom sources based on a plain-English ICP description. The output is a structured table: one row per contact, columns for every data point you'll need downstream.


What you want at this stage:


- **Name and company** (obvious, but confirm both are present)
- **Job title** that matches your ICP persona
- **Company size and industry** for segmentation
- **A signal field** if you have one — funding round, tech stack, open job posting, recent hire


Don't import a raw, unenriched list into Instantly. You'll burn send volume on contacts you can't personalize and emails that bounce.


---


## Step 2: Why Do You Need to Enrich Every Contact Before Export?


Enrichment fills in the gaps. You might have a name and company from a LinkedIn search but no verified email, no direct phone, no firmographic context. Enrichment tools resolve those gaps by querying multiple data providers and returning the best available result.


The fields that matter most for cold email:


Field Why It Matters in Instantly


Verified email Prevents bounces; protects domain reputation


First name Required for` {{firstName}}` personalization


Job title Drives persona-based messaging


Company name Required for` {{companyName}}` variable


Industry / vertical Enables segment-specific campaigns


Company size Helps you match messaging to company stage


Custom signal (e.g., tech stack, funding) Powers hyper-relevant opening lines


A[data enrichment agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/data-enrichment-agent) can run this enrichment automatically across your entire list — pulling verified emails, firmographics, funding data, and tech stack signals without you touching each row manually.


One thing worth saying plainly: **waterfall enrichment** — querying multiple providers in sequence until a valid result is found — significantly improves the fill rate on verified emails compared to a single-source lookup. According to Instantly's own documentation, unverified or incomplete contact data is the leading cause of campaign deliverability problems. If your enrichment tool only queries one provider, you'll leave a lot of contacts without verified emails, and those contacts either don't get imported or bounce when they do.


---


## Step 3: Why Does Email Verification Matter Before Importing to Instantly?


Enrichment tools return emails they believe are valid. Verification confirms they actually exist and will accept mail.


A bounce rate above 3% signals to inbox providers that you're sending to bad lists, according to[Instantly's deliverability guidelines](https://help.instantly.ai/en/articles/6786677-how-to-improve-your-email-deliverability) . Sustained high bounces damage your sending domain's reputation, which tanks deliverability across all your campaigns — not just the one that caused the problem.


Before you export to Instantly:


1. Run your enriched list through email verification (many enrichment tools include this; if yours doesn't, use a dedicated verifier)
2. Remove or flag any email marked invalid, catch-all, or unverifiable
3. Only import addresses marked valid or accept-all (with accept-all, expect some risk and keep volume lower)


If you're using Orange Slice, email verification happens as part of the enrichment step — you're not running a separate tool or paying twice.


---


## Step 4: Should You Segment Before or After Export?


Before. Always before.


Once leads are in Instantly and sequences have started, re-segmenting is painful. You can pause campaigns and move contacts, but it creates gaps in send schedules and complicates reporting. Segment in your enrichment tool *before* export.


Common segmentation approaches:


- **By ICP tier** — your best-fit accounts versus second-tier prospects
- **By persona** — VP Sales versus Head of RevOps versus Founder
- **By company size** — SMB, mid-market, enterprise each get different messaging
- **By buying signal** — contacts who triggered a signal (funding, hiring, tech change) versus cold contacts with no signal


Each segment becomes a separate CSV export and a separate Instantly campaign. That lets you write messaging that speaks directly to one person in one situation, which is the only way cold email works at scale.


See the[use cases hub](https://www.orangeslice.ai/use-cases) for examples of how different ICP segments map to different outbound plays.


---


## Step 5: How Do You Export Leads from an Enrichment Tool into Instantly?


You have two options: CSV import or direct integration.


### Option A: CSV Export


Every enrichment tool can export a CSV. In Instantly, you go to your campaign, click "Import Leads," and upload the file. Instantly maps your column headers to its lead fields and to personalization variables in your sequence steps.


**What to check before uploading:**


- Column headers are clean (no special characters, no spaces — use` first_name` not` First Name (verified)` )
- No duplicate emails across campaigns you're already running
- No emails you've previously unsubscribed or bounced


**What to do in Instantly after upload:**


- Map columns to Instantly's standard fields (first name, last name, email, company)
- Confirm custom columns appear as available variables in the sequence editor
- Spot-check five rows to confirm data populated correctly


### Option B: Direct Integration


If your enrichment tool has a native Instantly connector, use it. Orange Slice exports directly to Instantly — you select the campaign, choose which rows to push, and the contacts land in Instantly without a file download. This matters when you're running enrichment on a schedule or reacting to a buying signal: the gap between identifying a prospect and enrolling them in a sequence shrinks from hours to seconds.


For tools without a native connector, you can bridge with Zapier or Make. Set a trigger (new row in spreadsheet, new contact in CRM) and an action (add lead to Instantly campaign). It works, but every middleware hop is a potential failure point and adds latency.


---


## Step 6: How Do You Build Sequences That Actually Use Enrichment Data?


Enrichment only pays off if your sequences actually use it. An email that says "Hi {{firstName}}, I wanted to reach out about {{companyName}}" is not personalization — it's mail merge from 2009.


Use your enrichment fields to write opening lines that are specific:


- **Funding signal** : "Saw \[Company\] just closed a Series B — congrats. Teams scaling post-raise usually run into \[specific problem\]..."
- **Tech stack** : "Noticed you're running \[Tool\] — most teams using it hit \[specific friction point\] around \[scale threshold\]..."
- **Hiring signal** : "You're hiring a \[Role\] right now, which usually means \[inference about business problem\]..."


In Instantly's sequence editor, these fields appear as variables you drag into the email body. The variable name must exactly match the column header from your export. If your CSV column is` recent_funding_round` , your variable in Instantly is` {{recent_funding_round}}` .


---


## Step 7: How Do You Automate the Full Enrichment-to-Instantly Pipeline?


Running this manually once is fine. Running it at scale, repeatedly, with fresh signals feeding new leads every week, requires automation.


A fully automated enrichment-to-Instantly pipeline looks like this:


1. **Trigger** : A new company matches your ICP criteria (funding event, hiring signal, tech change)
2. **Agent action** : Lead generation agent finds the right contact at that company
3. **Enrichment** : Data enrichment agent fills in verified email, firmographics, signal fields
4. **Qualification** : Lead qualification agent scores the contact against your ICP and filters out poor fits
5. **Export** : Approved leads push directly to the correct Instantly campaign
6. **Sequence starts** : Instantly enrolls the contact and begins sending


This is what[GTM workflow automation](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/workflows) enables — a pipeline where a human defines the ICP and the messaging, and the agents handle the rest. The[agents overview](https://www.orangeslice.ai/agents) explains how these components work together.


Orange Slice supports this kind of end-to-end flow. It is not the right tool if you need deep CRM workflow automation or want to manage complex multi-channel sequences — Instantly handles the sequencing, and a dedicated[CRM agent](https://www.orangeslice.ai/product/crm-agent) handles sync back to HubSpot or Salesforce. Orange Slice's job is the top of that pipeline: finding, enriching, qualifying, and pushing leads to wherever they need to go next.


---


## Common Mistakes That Break the Pipeline


**Importing without verification.** Your enrichment tool's confidence score is not a substitute for verification. Always verify before import.


**Using the same campaign for all segments.** One campaign, one message, one persona. Mixing segments forces you to write to nobody.


**Ignoring column naming conventions.** Instantly's variable system is case-sensitive and space-sensitive. Clean your headers before export.


**Enriching once and never refreshing.** Contacts change jobs. Emails go stale. If a list is more than 90 days old, re-verify before re-using it.


**Over-indexing on volume.** A smaller list of highly enriched, well-segmented contacts outperforms a massive list of bare-minimum records. Instantly's deliverability infrastructure is excellent — don't waste it on bad data.


---


## What to Do Right Now


If you don't have an enrichment-to-Instantly pipeline yet, start with one segment. Pick your highest-priority ICP, build a list of 100–200 contacts, enrich them fully, verify emails, and import into a single Instantly campaign with one sequence. Measure reply rate and bounce rate. Then automate what you just did manually.
